title: DZNE Longitudinal Cognitive Impairment and Dementia Study with focus on stage 2 of the Alzheimer Continuum
summary: Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia. In recent years, significant progress has been made in the diagnosis and treatment of this disease. However, there are still many questions that need to be answered, particularly regarding the very early stages of the disease, in order to make treatment options even more effective. With the DELCODE 2 research project, the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) therefore aims to examine individuals with and without memory impairments over an extended period of time at regular intervals using various methods. The goal is to improve early detection and prognosis of potential Alzheimer’s disease.

interventions.name: The annual examinations conducted as part of the study take place over a period of 5 years and include, among others, detailed interviews with a study physician, neuropsychological assessments (evaluation of memory functions and other areas of cognitive performance), blood draws, and imaging examina

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Informed consent
• Meets the defined criteria for SCD, MCI, or the control group
• 60 years of age or older
• Sufficient knowledge of the German language to participate in all aspects of the study
• Presence of an informant (not applicable to the control group) (Definition of “informant”: The informant preferably lives with the participant and is defined as a person who spends at least four hours per day with the participant on at least four days per week and is able to assess the participant’s daytime and nighttime behavior.)
Exclusion criteria:
• Conditions that may explain SCD or MCI (other than Alzheimer’s disease)
• Cognitive impairments occurring in the context of a COVID-19 infection
• Current mental health conditions
• History of schizophrenia, alcohol dependence (within the last 3 years), or ADHD
• Known current neurological disorders of the brain
• Conditions that will require intensive treatment in the foreseeable future (e.g., cancers with planned treatment, planned TEP surgery)
• Conditions that are expected to lead to death within a maximum of 3 years
• Vision and/or hearing impairments that interfere with the performance of the examinations
• Long-term use of medications known to impair cognition
• MRI exclusion criteria
